skill.description: Guides Caffeine AI applications through Internet Identity authentication, role-based authorization, protected profiles, verified attributes, and secure frontend session handling.
skill.summary: Implement Caffeine AI authentication and role-based access control across Motoko backends and React frontends.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: All 67 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, fixed imports, documentation links, and identity terminology. A separate high-severity bootstrap risk remains because the first authenticated user automatically becomes administrator without an allowlist or secret.

remediation.issue: The first authenticated user automatically receives the administrator role.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit administrator principal, deployment allowlist, or one-time bootstrap secret before granting the initial administrator role.

semantic_findings.title: First Login Receives Administrator Role
semantic_findings.description: The documented bootstrap grants administrator access to the first authenticated user without a token or allowlist. An unintended early login could take control of a new deployment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The behavior is stated twice and explicitly requires no token or secret. The takeover risk depends only on deployment exposure before the intended administrator signs in.

content.user_title: Add Role-Based Authorization to Caffeine Apps
content.value_statement: Applications with private data need consistent authentication and authorization controls. This skill provides backend guards, profile protection, verified attributes, and frontend session patterns.
actual_capabilities: Integrates the Caffeine AI authorization mixin into a Motoko actor.
Defines administrator, user, and guest roles with permission checks.
Protects profile read and write methods using caller-aware backend guards.
Captures verified Internet Identity name, email, and SSO attributes.
Guides React login, logout, session restoration, and cache clearing behavior.
Explains migration steps for version 1 authorization dependencies.
limitations: Applies to Caffeine AI projects using Motoko, React, and Internet Identity.
Depends on the caffeineai-authorization and core-infrastructure packages.
Does not design custom username and password authentication.
The default first-login administrator bootstrap requires careful deployment control.

use_cases.title: Protect a New Caffeine Application
use_cases.description: Add authentication, role checks, protected profiles, and login state handling to a new application.

use_cases.title: Review Existing Authorization
use_cases.description: Check public Motoko methods for caller guards, ownership checks, administrator restrictions, and safe error handling.

use_cases.title: Upgrade Authorization Dependencies
use_cases.description: Move an existing project to version 1 packages and update the authorization mixin callback.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Authorization
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Caffeine AI authorization to my Motoko backend. Include the authorization mixin and protect authenticated profile methods.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner is adding access control to a new project.

prompt_templates.title: Build the Login Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React login flow using Internet Identity. Handle initialization, active login, restored sessions, logout, and query cache clearing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A frontend developer needs reliable authentication state.

prompt_templates.title: Protect Role-Based Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these backend methods and add administrator, user, or ownership checks. Explain the required role for each public operation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is securing an existing backend API.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate and Harden Authorization
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade this project to authorization version 1. Preserve verified attributes, audit every public method, and replace first-login administrator bootstrap with an allowlist.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced maintainer needs migration and security hardening.

output_examples.input: Protect profile access so users can edit themselves and administrators can view other profiles.
output: Caller-aware profile methods with user permission checks.
An ownership or administrator check for viewing another profile.
Clear authorization failures for rejected operations.

output_examples.input: Fix login behavior after a stored Internet Identity session is restored.
output: Authenticated content is gated by the restored authentication state.
Login controls remain disabled while the identity client initializes.
Logout clears cached application data and profile information.

output_examples.input: Upgrade the existing authorization integration to version 1.
output: Updated backend and frontend dependency requirements.
The authorization mixin receives its required second argument.
Verified attribute handling is added only when the application needs it.

best_practices: Enforce authorization in backend methods even when the frontend hides restricted controls.
Use caller identity and ownership checks for every personal data operation.
Clear cached private data immediately when a user logs out.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on frontend visibility as the only authorization control.
Do not use interactive login success to detect restored sessions.
Do not grant the initial administrator role without controlled bootstrap conditions.

faq.question: Which roles does this skill describe?
faq.answer: It describes administrator, user, and guest roles provided by the authorization package.

faq.question: Does it support Internet Identity?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers login state, restored sessions, principals, and verified identity attributes.

faq.question: Can it capture a verified email address?
faq.answer: Yes. The authorization mixin can pass verified email data to an application callback.

faq.question: Does it replace backend permission checks?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns for applying permission, ownership, and administrator checks to backend methods.

faq.question: Can I use custom authentication instead?
faq.answer: Yes. Remove the authorization package and its related imports, state, mixin, and guards before implementing the replacement.

faq.question: What is the main deployment risk?
faq.answer: The default bootstrap makes the first authenticated user an administrator. Restrict deployment access or configure an explicit administrator.
